To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha mRNA and protein are overexpressed in the vast majority of CC-RCCC; (ii) this is due to both VHL-dependent and VHL-independent processes; (iii) HIF-2 alpha is overexpressed more than HIF-1 alpha in RCC; and (iv) HIF overexpression in RCC is associated with increased VEGF expression, increased microvessel count, and poor survival.
HIFis expressed in the majority of renal cell carcinoma (RCC) and the expression of HIFA is biased towards the HIF-1 isoform.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to understanding the development of a new therapeutic target.
the role of the von Hipp el-Lindau ( VHL) tumor suppressor protein in the pathogenesis of renal cell carcinomas.
the molecular mechanisms underlying tumor development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VHL gene is a tumor suppressor gene in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

the VHL gene is mutated in most cases of renal cell carcinoma (RCC), but that this mutation is not sufficient to cause RCC, but that it is required for the development of clear cell RCC, which is by far the most common histologic subtype.
HIF-2α is a marker for RCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

VHL mutations in renal cell cancer lead to stabilization of the HIF-1 and HIF-2 transcription factor complexes, which in turn upregulate expression of the angiogenic growth factor, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF).
VHL-deficient RCCs are hypoxic and that this hypoxia leads to the activation of HIFs.
VHL mutations lead to increased HIF-2 expression and that increased HIF- 2 expression leads to increased expression of VEGF and increased angiogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VHL protein is a substrate adaptor protein that recognizes HIF as a substrate for degradation.
HIF-1 and HIF-2 are expressed in different patterns in different tumors and different tissues.
the HIF pathway plays a role in the development of clear cell renal cancer.
